Constitution of UNT Robotics
ARTICLE I – Organization Name and Mission
Section 1: Name
The official name of this organization shall be UNT Robotics
The organization may also refer to itself as Robotics
Section 2: Mission
The purpose of UNT Robotics is to help UNT undergraduate students and graduate students pursue their interest in robotics with a hands-on and collaborative experience in designing, building, and programming robots and mechatronics.
ARTICLE II – Governing Rules and Regulations
This organization shall comply with all University policies (including the Code of Student Conduct) and procedures, as well as local, state, and federal laws.
The most current version of Robert's Rules of Order shall be the parliamentary authority for all matters of procedure not specifically covered by this constitution.
ARTICLE III – Membership
Section 1: Membership Statement
Membership in this organization is limited to any student service fee paying student who is currently enrolled at the University of North Texas.
Membership is open to all students without regard to race, color, national or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, political affiliation, disability, marital status, ancestry, genetic information, citizenship, or veteran status.
Section 2: Additional Membership Requirements
There are no additional requirements
Together with Article III, Section 1, these additional requirements define what it means to be an “active student member.”
Section 3: Voting Rights
A. Any member on the roster at the time of the election is eligible to vote in the election.
B. A member can become registered by submitting a document containing their name, EUID, and email.
ARTICLE IV – Officers
Section 1: Eligibility
To be eligible to serve as an officer of this organization, an active student member shall possess (at the time of election and during their term of office) at least the minimum requirements regarding enrollment, GPA, and disciplinary standing as stated in UNT Policy 07.019 (Student Organization Policy).
An active student member who fails to meet any one of the requirements is automatically ineligible to serve as an officer until all criteria are met.
Section 3: Titles and Duties
The officers of this organization shall include a President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary, Webmaster, Public Relations, Inventory, Event Coordinator, and Project Manager.
The President shall:
Serve as the official representative of the organization.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of the organization.
Serve as the liaison between the organization and University community.
Call regular and special meetings and presides over meetings of the organization.
Prepare agendas for meetings.
Maintain communication with Student Activities and ensure that all organizational information, including registration, is current.
Ensure that all officers are performing their duties as defined in this Constitution.
Keep advisor informed of activities and functions of the organization.
Be familiar with UNT policies (especially 07.019 Student Organization Policy and the Code of Student Conduct) as they relate to student organizations and communicate them to the organization as needed.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected President.
Oversee new member education
The Vice President shall:
Assist the President in their duties.
Assume the President’s responsibilities in their absence.
Keep accurate records of all meetings in the Secretary’s absence.
Plan and be responsible for all retreats and training of the organization.
Perform an audit of all financial transactions of the organization once per semester.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected Vice President.
Assist in special projects as assigned by the President.
D. The Treasurer shall:
Keep an accurate account of all funds received and expended.
Present a budget report of deposits and expenditures to the membership at least once per month, and as requested by the President, Vice President, advisor, or Student Activities.
Be responsible for collecting dues and notifying members who are delinquent in their payments, if applicable.
Provide financial records sufficient to allow the Vice President to perform audits.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected Treasurer.
Assist in special projects as assigned by the President.
E. The Secretary shall:
Notify members of meetings at least 48 hours in advance.
Keep accurate minutes and records of all meetings.
Maintain an accurate list of members and their contact information.
Prepare the organization’s registration profile and submit to Student Activities at the beginning of each semester, and when there are changes in organizational information over the course of the semester.
Take attendance at all meetings and maintain an attendance record.
Check eligibility for potential officers, prior to annual elections.
Keep copy of constitution and have available for members.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected Secretary.
Assist in special projects as assigned by the President.
F. Webmaster
Maintaining website and digital assets
This position is appointed
G. Public Relations
Responsible for all social media content.
Establish and maintain contact with outside organizations.
Oversee advertising for the organization.
In charge of eagle mail distributions
H. Inventory
Maintain a list of the organization’s physical inventory.
Check items out to members.
Oversee that all parts are returned to the organization locker at the end of the semester.
Oversee fining members for lost or damaged parts.
I.Event Coordinator
Hosts and organizes events at the president’s discretion.
J. Project Manager
Leads projects at the president’s discretion.
Section 4: Elections
The nomination and election of officers shall occur annually at the membership meeting held in May.
Any active student member may nominate someone or themselves for office.
All active student members present will have the opportunity to vote by secret ballot.
A candidate shall be elected by a majority of votes.
If no candidate receives a majority of votes, the top two candidates will immediately enter into a run-off election.
The positions of Webmaster and Project Manager are chosen by committee.
Section 5: Installation and Term of Office
Newly elected officers shall take office the fall following the membership meeting in May and their term will end immediately following the membership meeting the next Fall.
Any change in officer information should be reported to Student Activities.
The length of term of office shall be no longer than one year.
Section 6: Vacancies
Removal
Leadership may be revoked without mutual agreement for non-participation, misconduct, failure to fulfill job duties, violation of any provision of the Constitution, or for any action or conduct that is deemed detrimental to the welfare of the organization, members, or the University of North Texas.
A petition to remove the officer in question must be submitted to the President (or Vice President in the event the officer in question is the President). Such a petition must contain the signature of at least a majority of the active student members of the organization. When such a petition is received, the President (or Vice President) shall call a meeting of the organization to decide upon removal.
The officer in question will be notified in writing of the grounds for removal at least one week prior to the meeting and will be allowed to address the organization in order to relate to members any relevant defense prior to the voting for removal.
An officer may be removed from office upon a 2/3 affirmative vote of active student members.
Resignation-The resignation of an officer must be submitted to the President (or Vice President if the President is resigning) and advisor at least two (2) weeks in advance.
Filling Vacancies
The nomination and election process as stated in Article III, Section 4 will take place at the next membership meeting.
The newly elected officers’ term shall end at the annual installation of officers in May as Article III, Section 5 above.
Article V: Meetings
Section 1: Membership Meetings
Membership meetings shall be held biweekly during the academic school year.
Meetings are open to those defined in Article III.
Officers and active student members are allowed one vote per motion.
The quorum required to conduct business is a majority of the officers.
Unless otherwise stated in this constitution, a motion is considered passed with a majority vote.
Section 2: Officer Meetings
Officer meetings shall be held weekly during the academic school year.
Meetings are open to those defined in Article III.
Officers are allowed one vote per motion.
The quorum required to conduct business is a majority of the officers.
Unless otherwise stated in this constitution, a motion is considered passed with a majority vote.
Section 3: Special Meetings
Special meetings may be called by the President, with the approval of the officers. A majority vote of the officers or active student members may also call a special meeting.
The Secretary will be responsible for notifying all members and/or officers at least 48 hours in advance, by e-mail and/or telephone.
Article VI: Advisor
Section 1: Eligibility and Selection
The advisor shall be selected by the officers.
To be eligible to serve as the advisor, the person must be a full-time UNT faculty or staff member.
The advisor has no term limit as long as they remain eligible.
Section 2: Expectations
Perform the responsibilities listed in UNT Policy 07.019 (Student Organization Policy).
Has no voting rights within the organization.
Be available to officers and members for consultation, advice, counsel, and as a resource.
Be familiar with and provide guidance on university policies and Student Activities procedures pertaining to student organizations.
Meet regularly with the President.
Sign and/or approve required Student Activities and university paperwork.
Attend the organization’s meetings and activities when necessary.
Keep open lines of communication with Student Activities on matters of concern, regarding the student organization.
Section 3: Removal and Vacancy
If the organization wishes to remove the advisor, the advisor will be notified in writing of the possible removal at least 72 hours prior to the vote and will be allowed to address the officers in order to relate any relevant defense prior to the voting for removal.
Upon a majority vote of officers, the advisor will be removed from their duties.
In the event that an advisor is removed or resigns, a new advisor shall be elected within 15 school days. A change in advisor information should be immediately reported to Student Activities.
ARTICLE VII – Finances
Section 1: Dues
Dues and other fees, as well as the collection schedule, may be set by a majority vote of active student members.
Section 2: Payment
Organizational funds may be spent on items such as office supplies, events and activities, publicity, travel expenses, and conference fees, but will not be used for anything illegal under University policy or local, state, and federal laws.
The Treasurer and President shall be responsible for ensuring the payment of all debts accumulated by the organization.
Section 3: Transition
It shall be the responsibility of all account signers to change contact information, as well as assist in the update of new account signatures with the organization’s financial institution, after each election.
Section 4: Dissolution
In the event that the organization ceases to exist, any funds remaining in the organization’s bank account shall be set aside by the University of North Texas by the advisor.
ARTICLE VIII – Statement of Non-Hazing
As defined in state law (Texas Education Code 37.151-157) and University policy, this organization will not engage in hazing, participate in hazing, or commit any act that causes or is likely to cause bodily danger, physical harm, or personal degradation or disgrace resulting in physical or mental harm to any fellow student or person attending the institution.
Article IX – Amendments
An amendment to the constitution may be proposed by any active student member of the organization, and must be submitted in writing to the President.
The proposed amendment shall be announced at an officer meeting at least one weeks prior to the meeting when the vote will be taken.
The day the proposed amendment has been announced, the organization may vote to adopt the amendment by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of active officers.
History of Constitution
Created: November 9, 2018
Revised: April 24, 2019

Constitution of UNT Robotics
ARTICLE I – Organization Name and Mission
Section 1: Name
The official name of this organization shall be UNT Robotics
The organization may also refer to itself as Robotics
Section 2: Mission
The purpose of UNT Robotics is to help UNT undergraduate students and graduate students pursue their interest in robotics with a hands-on and collaborative experience in designing, building, and programming robots and mechatronics.
ARTICLE II – Governing Rules and Regulations
This organization shall comply with all University policies (including the Code of Student Conduct) and procedures, as well as local, state, and federal laws.
The most current version of Robert's Rules of Order shall be the parliamentary authority for all matters of procedure not specifically covered by this constitution.
ARTICLE III – Membership
Section 1: Membership Statement
Membership in this organization is limited to any student service fee paying student who is currently enrolled at the University of North Texas.
Membership is open to all students without regard to race, color, national or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, political affiliation, disability, marital status, ancestry, genetic information, citizenship, or veteran status.
Section 2: Additional Membership Requirements
A member of good standing is defined as a member who has paid their dues to the organization. A club member can become a member of good standing at anytime during the semester.
Dues are paid per semester on an individual basis. Dues as assigned by the incoming executive board. If a member is unable to pay the full dues amount, a payment plan or alternative payment methods may be enacted by the treasurer or president.
Dues will begin collection at the first org meeting and will continue through the entirety of the semester.
Together with Article III, Section 1, these additional requirements define what it means to be an “active student member.”
Section 3: Voting Rights
Voting is open to all members of good standing.
Members who are not in good standing can participate in discussions, but will not be able to vote.
ARTICLE IV – Officers
Section 1: Eligibility
To be eligible to serve as an officer of this organization, an active student member shall possess (at the time of election and during their term of office) at least the minimum requirements regarding enrollment, GPA, and disciplinary standing as stated in UNT Policy 07.019 (Student Organization Policy).
An active student member who fails to meet any one of the requirements is automatically ineligible to serve as an officer until all criteria are met.
To be eligible to be nominated for an executive position you must be a member of good standing
Section 2: Titles and DutiesThe officers of this organization shall include a President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, Public Relations, Inventory Manager, Event Coordinator.
The President shall:
Serve as the official representative of the organization.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of the organization.
Serve as the liaison between the organization and University community.
Call regular and special meetings and presides over meetings of the organization.
Maintain communication with Student Activities and ensure that all organizational information, including registration, is current.
Ensure that all officers are performing their duties as defined in this Constitution.
Keep advisor informed of activities and functions of the organization.
Be familiar with UNT policies (especially 07.019 Student Organization Policy and the Code of Student Conduct) as they relate to student organizations and communicate them to the organization as needed.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected President.
Oversee workshops and lesson plans.
The Vice President shall:
Assist the President in their duties.
Assume the President’s responsibilities in their absence.
Keep accurate records of all meetings in the Secretary’s absence.
Plan and be responsible for all retreats and training of the organization.
Perform an audit of all financial transactions of the organization once per semester.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected Vice President.
D. The Treasurer shall:
Keep an accurate account of all funds received and expended.
Present a budget report of deposits and expenditures to the membership at least once per month, and as requested by the President, Vice President, advisor, or Student Activities.
Be responsible for collecting dues
Provide financial records sufficient to allow the Vice President to perform audits.
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected Treasurer.
Any assets coming in or out of the organization will be managed and released by the Treasurer.
Treasurer will maintain a list of all members in good standing.
Club funds will all be managed in the central org bank account. All purchases or removal of funds must have prior approval based on the criteria below.
Funds not for a specific project, effort, or budget are considered general funds and will require Treasurer approval for purchases below 50 dollars. The President must be notified of every purchase and retains the right to veto. If vetoed the purchase can go to the members in good standing for a vote. Anything above 50 will be put to a general vote to be used.
Funds can be allocated to discretionary accounts either through fundraising or donations that are specific to the effort or project. (I.E. go-fund-me funds or UNT department funding for a specific competition). All funds raised will still go to the organizations bank account and be managed by the Treasurer. Any funds received must contain an explicit plan for the remaining funds post completion of the intended use. If there is not a requirement set by the donor of the money, remaining funds will go to the general funds account.
Alternatively funds can be allocated to a discretionary account though a proposed budget. The budget should first be approved by the exec board then sent to vote, where the members will vote on what portions will be approved or disapproved. This must be done through an itemized list of parts and can receive all, partial, or no funding based on the results of the vote.
Funds in a discretionary account still require Treasurer approval and retain president veto power but have a max limit of 300 per purchase. Anything greater requires a general vote.
Expanding allocated funds or budgets requires a general vote .
E. The Secretary shall:
Prepare agendas for meetings.
Notify members of meetings at least 48 hours in advance.
Keep accurate minutes and records of all meetings.
Maintain an accurate list of members and their contact information.
Prepare the organization’s registration profile and submit to Student Activities at the beginning of each semester, and when there are changes in organizational information over the course of the semester.
Take attendance at all meetings and maintain an attendance record.
Check eligibility for potential officers, prior to annual elections.
Keep copy of constitution and have available for members.
Summarize meetings
Provide all documents and records pertaining to their responsibilities to the newly-elected Secretary.
G. Public Relations
Responsible for all social media content.
Establish and maintain contact with outside organizations.
Oversee advertising for the organization.
In charge of eagle mail distributions.
Assist the President with UNT and 3rd party meetings.
H. Inventory
Maintain a list of the organization’s physical inventory.
Check items out to members.
Oversee that all parts are returned to the organization locker at the end of the semester.
Oversee fining members for lost or damaged parts.
Oversee any space the organization is maintaining and its upkeep.
I.Event Coordinator
Responsible for hosting and organizing organization events at the president’s discretion.
Responsible for understanding and following all University event policy.
Manage University Competition/s
Oversee and organize the workshops
Reserving rooms and acquiring materials for general meetings
Section 3: Elections
The nomination and election of officers shall occur annually at least four weeks prior to the last eligible day to hold meetings of the spring semester.
Any active student member may nominate someone or themselves for office.
All members of good standing present will have the opportunity to vote by secret ballot.
A candidate shall be elected by a majority of votes.
If no candidate receives a majority of votes, the top two candidates will immediately enter into a run-off election.
New chair positions are appointed by the new officers.
Section 4: Installation and Term of Office
Newly elected executive board members will take office immediately after the last day the school policy allows the organization to hold a meeting.
During the time between elections and the newly elected executive board members taking office, newly elected board members will be allowed to participate in future planning, so long as they do not inhibit the current acting board.
Any change in officer information should be reported to Student Activities.
The length of term of office shall be no longer than one year.
Presidents can only serve one term.
Section 5: Vacancies
Removal
Leadership may be revoked without mutual agreement for non-participation, misconduct, failure to fulfill job duties, violation of any provision of the Constitution, or for any action or conduct that is deemed detrimental to the welfare of the organization, members, or the University of North Texas.
A petition to remove the officer in question must be submitted to the President (or Vice President in the event the officer in question is the President). Such a petition must contain the signatures of at least a majority of the members of good standing or a majority of executive board members. When such a petition is received, the President (or Vice President) shall call a meeting of the organization to decide upon removal.
The officer in question will be notified in writing of the grounds for removal at least one week prior to the meeting and will be allowed to address the organization in order to relate to members any relevant defense prior to the voting for removal.
An officer may be removed from office upon a 2/3 affirmative vote of members of good standing or officers.
Resignation-The resignation of an officer must be submitted to the President (or Vice President if the President is resigning) and advisor at least two (2) weeks in advance.
Filling Vacancies
The nomination and election process as stated in Article IV, Section 3 will take place at the next membership meeting.
The newly elected officers’ term shall end at the annual installation of officers on the last day organizations are able to hold meetings as defined by the University.
Article V: Meetings
Section 1: Membership Meetings
Membership meetings shall be held biweekly during the academic school year.
Meetings are open to those defined in Article III section 1.
Officers and members of good standing are allowed one vote per motion.
The quorum required to conduct business is a majority of the officers.
Unless otherwise stated in this constitution, a motion is considered passed with a majority vote.
Section 2: Officer Meetings
Officer meetings shall be held weekly during the academic school year.
Meetings are open to those defined as officers in Article IV and invited guests.
Officers are allowed one vote per motion.
The quorum required to conduct business is a majority of the officers.
Unless otherwise stated in this constitution, a motion is considered passed with a majority vote.
Section 3: Special Meetings
Special meetings may be called by the President, with the approval of the officers. A majority vote of the officers or members of good standing may also call a special meeting.
The Secretary will be responsible for notifying all members and/or officers at least 48 hours in advance, by email and/or telephone.
Article VI: Advisor
Section 1: Eligibility and Selection
The advisor shall be selected by the officers.
To be eligible to serve as the advisor, the person must be a full-time UNT faculty or staff member.
The advisor has no term limit as long as they remain eligible.
Section 2: Expectations
Perform the responsibilities listed in UNT Policy 07.019 (Student Organization Policy).
Has no voting rights within the organization.
Be available to officers and members for consultation, advice, counsel, and as a resource.
Be familiar with and provide guidance on university policies and Student Activities procedures pertaining to student organizations.
Meet regularly with the President.
Sign and/or approve required Student Activities and university paperwork.
Attend the organization’s meetings and activities when necessary.
Keep open lines of communication with Student Activities on matters of concern, regarding the student organization.
Section 3: Removal and Vacancy
If the organization wishes to remove the advisor, the advisor will be notified in writing of the possible removal at least 72 hours prior to the vote and will be allowed to address the officers in order to relate any relevant defense prior to the voting for removal.
Upon a majority vote of officers, the advisor will be removed from their duties.
In the event that an advisor is removed or resigns, a new advisor shall be elected within 15 school days. A change in advisor information should be immediately reported to Student Activities.
ARTICLE VII – Finances
Section 1: Dues
Dues and other fees, as well as the collection schedule, may be set by a majority vote of the officers.
Section 2: Payment
Organizational funds may be spent on items such as office supplies, events and activities, publicity, travel expenses, and conference fees, but will not be used for anything illegal under University policy or local, state, and federal laws.
The Treasurer and President shall be responsible for ensuring the payment of all debts accumulated by the organization.
Section 3: Transition
It shall be the responsibility of all account signers to change contact information, as well as assist in the update of new account signatures with the organization’s financial institution, after each election.
Section 4: Dissolution
In the event that the organization ceases to exist, any funds remaining in the organization’s bank account shall be set aside by the University of North Texas by the advisor.
ARTICLE VIII – Statement of Non-Hazing
As defined in state law (Texas Education Code 37.151-157) and University policy, this organization will not engage in hazing, participate in hazing, or commit any act that causes or is likely to cause bodily danger, physical harm, or personal degradation or disgrace resulting in physical or mental harm to any fellow student or person attending the institution.
Article IX – Amendments
An amendment to the constitution may be proposed by any active student member of the organization, and must be submitted in writing to the President.
The proposed amendment shall be announced at an officer meeting at least one weeks prior to the meeting when the vote will be taken.
The day the proposed amendment has been announced, the organization may vote to adopt the amendment by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of active officers.
